comment: Chad is the MAN. While he may get off track in class about random things, he is super funny and loves his students. Some tedious homework and the tests are the biggest things to worry about in class, but if you take notes and do the practice exams, its hard not to get a good grade in the class. If you want to laugh while learning, take my dawg Chad

Dr. Curtis is one of the most caring professors I've had. He is genuinely curious about his students' lives and makes class enjoyable and engaging by making jokes throughout the sometimes mundane material. He is very accessible outside of class and only assigns a few homework assignments throughout the semester.

Curtis is a great professor, really nice guy. Sometimes class can feel boring but he is funny which makes it manageable. Minimal hw, and it's about 30% of final grade which makes it easy to do well. Exams are really fair and predictable. Overall learned a lot and happy with the class. Great guy great prof.

Very kind and funny professor. Gets off topic a lot in class talking to students. However, lectures can be very confusing since there isn't a textbook to follow. I don't felt like I learned that much in the class, however, it's fairly easy. About 6 problem sets all semester and three tests.

very kind and caring professor, makes an effort to get to know all of his students. his lectures are kind of confusing and i wish there was a textbook or other course material to follow, but he has lots of office hours and is always willing to help clarify. great guy would recommend for macro

One of the best professors I've had, wait til spring and take him for macro theory. He's such a great professor and person, he really gets to know all of his students. His tests aren't too bad and only hw is 5 problem sets, although they're tough. He lectures all class which can get boring but he makes the most of it. Can't recommend him enough.
Very easy professor for macro, but not great if you actually want to learn anything. Problem sets can be confusing sometimes but he is always available during office hours to answer questions.
An easy class with a pretty nice professor, but if you actually want to learn anything I'd go with someone else.
He's a great guy who knows how to teach. The homework is a bit long and technical but the tests are easier. Definitely take him for easy macro.

if you know nothing about macro, you're gonna have a hard time with his guy. he makes lectures complicated sometimes and doesnt take things slow. I put more effort into understanding lessons and HOURS on problem sets. The problem sets do prepare you for tests. He focuses a lot on the math/graph side. not the worst, not the best.

Very knowledgeable about all things Econ. This is a heavily math-based class(some concepts are mixed in but its mostly taught through math). Very engaging and always accessible outside of class. Homeworks are harder than the tests and really helps to better understand what he lectures on. Would definitely recommend taking his class.

I took Dr. Curtis for Econ102 and I am currently taking him for Econ272. He is so caring and nice, really passionate about the material and about his students. He always tries to get to know everyone and makes little inside jokes with the class. He is truly lovely. Assigns problem sets once every week or 2. Beware: he rly likes Google Earth.

So far, he is the only bschool professor I've had that seems to actually have an interest in his students' lives outside of class. His class is pretty straightforward, although his problem sets deviate somewhat from what was directly learned.

teaches with the socratic method so sometimes really hard to get an answer out of him on the homework. sometimes tests and homework can be hard because they're really elevated from whatever we learn in class

Good choice for Macro. Tries to incorporate real-world examples for everything. Sometimes spends too much time on Google Earth. Really tries to get to know every student and does his best to explain things if you ask questions. No textbook needed.

Professor Curtis is a great guy who I highly recommend. Class is based off of problem sets and tests but he defienlty prepares you for both if you go to class and pay attention. Also, he tries o make a subject many find boring to be entertaining.

Chad is a fantastic guy that deeply cares about his students. But I found the tests and problems sets to be overly focused on solving long algebraic equations, which meant there was much less time to discuss macroeconomic concepts and theories in detail.

Dr. Curtis is a great professor. He is nice, funny and very helpful. He gives a lot of unnecessary examples and stuffs but still gives you what you need for the problem sets and tests. The problem sets are long but easy. The tests are pretty much like the problem sets and fairly easy. He is an easy grader. Highly recommended.

Great guy who clearly loves what he does, but is not the best teacher. He uses full class length lectures with a bunch of unnecessary and untested information. Makes up for it by being an easy grader, but this does not guarantee an A but he is definitely a better choice than other macro professors.

Professor Curtis is pretty funny and he's a nice guy. He's willing to meet outside of class but don't expect much help. He's mostly there to use the Socratic method and ask you questions until you get the answer yourself. He has difficult problem sets that usually take a lot of time to finish but he's a more than fair grader. Overall pretty good.

Dr. Curtis is awesome. He always makes weird tangents and strange analogies, talked in a disturbingly excited way, and is just a joy to watch. He doesn't use a textbook but in class notes (or memory) is more than enough. He gives rough problem sets but makes sure that tests are fair. 100% take, because he's so much fun and is pretty easy.

Ultra mega super nice person. His class is fun and chill. The guy incorporates econ and geography in his lectures and assignment so you can learn a lot while analyzing the data. Even his homework is soooo enjoyable to work on. Tests are not hard; they cover what you have at class. Definitely recommend to take Curtis's!

Curtis is amazing. He is very smart and fairly young and connects well to his students. His lectures go pretty fast, but he is available during many office hours. You have no homework except for an extensive and sometimes difficult problem set packet due each week, but work with a group and you will be fine. Tests are hard but he is a fair grader.

Super nice guy. The material is not the easiest but it is not too difficult. He certainly does not go out of his way to make it hard. He makes you feel super comfortable in class and there are not a ton of assignments. All around a good professor.

I personally didn't like this class that much - I felt like I haven't learned anything substantial, especially for a macro class. But don't miss class, or you will be left with nothing but regrets and a terrible grade.
Always encouraging students and willing to help outside class. He tries to make the class interesting. Tests are not tough but assigns long problems sets.

Honestly he is one of the best professors I have had in UR. He really wants you to do well in the class and tries to help you understand the materials as easy as possible. For those of you thinking about taking Econ 102. Trust me, take him because you will not regret it

Dr. Curtis is amazing! I learned so much in this class. I'm not an econ major, but he makes the subject matter so accessible to all students that his class became one of my favorites. He's extremely helpful outside of class, and he's very funny. One of the best profs I've had at UR--take him if you get the chance!

Favorite professor so far! Class is always fun and interesting. Tests are a bit challenging but he grades very fairly. Always willing to help his students. Textbook not required so everything's covered in class! Great professor, always encouraging students! Definitely take him!

Dr. Curtis is a great professor! If you can get him, take him. His lectures are very clear, funny and interesting. He is very helpful, and wants what's best for his students. Test are hard, but if you study for them you will be fine. He often uses problems from the homework assignments on his tests.

i love dr. curtis! hes a new professor but he is def the nicest and the most understanding professor ive had so far. hes a fair grader and wants everyone to do well. not much homework at all, and all reading you have to do is one book and textbook is not required altho its helpful to have it as a reference. take him if you can!

Great guy. Wants his students to do well. But he is new and doesn't seem to have a solid lesson plan. The class is interesting and easy. Homework set once a week - takes an hour at most. Definitely has potential to be a great professor.

It was an easy class, but I think that was my issue with the course. I didn't feel like I understood macroeconomics by the end of the course. He's very funny, but classes are boring (heavy note-taking and lecture). However, he's very accessible outside class and his office hours are helpful. His problem sets aren't bad and the tests are very doable
All around great professor. Assignments prepare you adequately for exams and he does a good job of tying the material into current events. Would recommend every day of the week.

As his name suggests, Dr. Curtis is a CHAD. He's so friendly, and knowledgeable, and makes the class material much easier than it appears to be. He recommends a textbook but you do NOT need it AT ALL. A couple of problem sets and 2 midterms compose most of the grade so if you pay attention and study accordingly it should be an easy A.

Awesome teacher; doesn't use a textbook so it's clear that he wants you to know only the things done in class; long homework assignments but they help you learn and he helps with them a lot if you go to his office hours; tests are a different version of the homework assignments; one of my favorite classes and teachers
try to be funny, failed. Miss one class? good luck on homework.
